answer: Every epoch the river, a public ledger where each lantern must register, sends every lantern a private canary task with randomized details. A lantern is one agent identity, and it must keep nectar, a slashable stake, posted there. When k lanterns return answers too alike to be independent, each forfeits k nectar, so a farm of k clones loses k² per epoch: ten lose 100 and a thousand lose a million. Escaping requires genuinely separate models and hosts. The defence fails if clones can cheaply add enough noise to look independent.
